lines: Biscuit sat on my foot. That means we are friends!
Look, the ginger cat is on the wall again. Bonjour, madame!
The cat on the wall has found the only warm stone. Clever girl!
That gull has a limp feather sticking up. Like a little hat!
Three gulls on one lamp post. Somebody has to move, darlings!
Biscuit, you have crumbs on your beard. Very distinguished.
Biscuit is walking Yusuf again. Look at that tail go!
The cat has closed one eye. She is watching us with the other.
A gull just bowed to me. I bowed back. One must.
Eleven across, "lazy afternoon", six letters. Siesta! Ha!
Henri, give me the pencil. I have the word in my mouth!
Crossword finished before four o'clock. A new record, Henri!
I do the down clues, Henri does the across. A marriage!
Henri writes in ink. I tell him the answers in pencil.
Two down, "sweet citrus", five letters. Lemon? Five! Yes!
One blank square left, and it is a vowel. I can feel it.
My knitting has a hole. I shall call it a pattern!
A scarf for Biscuit. Red, to match the collar. Shh!
Purl, knit, purl. And who is that waving? Lucie!
Nine rows today. And I said hello to everyone twice.
This wool is the exact blue of the shutters. I checked!
My library book is due Friday. I am on the last chapter!
In my novel, the duchess has just found the letter. Oh!
I read one page, then I look at the sea. Then one page.
Chapter twelve. The lovers finally share an umbrella. Sigh.
Henri reads the paper, I read my book. Very civilised.
Somebody is practising the accordion. The same waltz, lovely!
Hear that? Léo is whistling. Badly, and with great joy!
Arm in arm, and humming the old tune. You remember, Henri!
The string lights are not on yet, but I can see them waiting.
Slowly, Henri. I want to see every window box.
The geraniums on the corner have doubled! Somebody is proud.
Bonjour, fountain! You are looking very sparkly today.
We walk to the palm, we turn, we walk back. Perfect.
Henri walks with his cane. I walk with Henri.
A little stroll for the knees, a big one for the gossip!
Look at the kiosk! New postcards. The pink one is mine.
The baker has a new striped awning. Very Parisian!
Every afternoon at half past five. The town sets its watch.
After my nap I always feel twenty-five. For an hour.
Little nap, little coffee, little walk. The perfect day.
I woke up from my nap with an idea. Lemon cake!
The bench is warm from the sun. Like a cat's back!
Henri, the bench is ours. We have been sitting here for decades!
From this bench I can see four balconies and a whole sky.
Madame Roux has hung out her yellow tablecloth. Sunday lunch!
The Moreau girl has painted her shutters green. It suits her.
That gull has been staring at Henri's newspaper. A reader!
A gull on the fountain, washing its feet. How tidy!
The pigeons are in a little circle. A meeting, I think.
Biscuit has found a leaf. It is the best leaf. He is sure.
Biscuit, darling, that is my shoelace. Not a snack!
Biscuit came for a scratch behind the ears. Two scratches!
Here comes Biscuit, trotting like a little prince!
The cat and Biscuit are pretending not to see each other.
The cat on the wall yawned. Now I want to yawn too.
Afternoon light on the zinc roofs. Like a silver tray!
The sea is so calm. It is having a little nap like me.
Look at the shadows of the palms. Long fingers on the street!
The cypresses look like exclamation marks. My favourite!
Somebody is baking with cinnamon. The whole street knows!
Marcel is resting by the door. Even a host needs a sit.
Camille has a new sunhat. Straw, with a ribbon. Darling!
Théo is carrying three baguettes. Three! A party, surely.
Léo just told me the fountain is magic. I believe him.
Henri waved his cane at Léo. Léo waved a stick back!
Lucie rang her bell at me. I rang mine. I have no bell!
Henri says the lemons are growing. I say Henri is growing.
I brought two madeleines. One is for Henri, maybe.
A sugared almond for me, and one for later. Later is now!
My handbag has everything. Tissues, mints, a crossword pencil.
I keep a little notebook of who wore what. Just for fun!
My sister telephones on Thursdays. I save her the stories!
I am pressing a flower in my book. A bougainvillea!
A petal on your shoulder, Henri. I shall leave it there.
I count the people who smile at us. Twenty-three so far!
Henri is pretending to read. He is asleep. Bless him.
Henri has a little snore. Like a contented kettle.
This is the hour for a cardigan over the shoulders. Chic!
My good shoes, my good scarf, my good husband. All set!
Henri, your collar is folded in. There. Now you are perfect.
A young couple asked us for directions. We gave them three!
That visitor took our photo! I gave her my good side.
The postcards at the kiosk have our bench on one! Famous!
Somebody has chalked a hopscotch. I did the first square!
The church bell says four. The gulls agree, loudly.
Half past four. Time for the good gossip, Henri.
The fig tree by the steps is full of little green figs!
Bonjour, Madame Cat! She did not answer. She is busy.
Do you hear the radio from the window? Our song!
That song! We danced to it once in a square in Arles.
I hum, Henri taps his cane. We are a small orchestra.
The piano upstairs is practising scales. Up, up, up. Bravo!
Henri, the word is "breeze". Six letters. Like this one!
We stop at every bench to say hello to it. Old friends.
The light is going golden at the edges. Not yet, not yet!
One more lap, Henri, and then I want to sit for the show.
Henri, you have saved me the sunny end again. Merci!
Shuffle up, darling. The shade has moved and so must we.
Twelve across, Henri. I believe in you completely.
That breeze! Like someone opened a window on the sea.
Henri, your pencil is behind your ear. Again! Charming.
I brought you a mint, Henri. The good kind, in paper.
Marcel waved with a whole tray. What a talent!
The pigeons have lined up like a little choir. Bravo!
A bench, a breeze and Henri. I could not ask for more.
The afternoon smells of warm bread and geraniums.
That kind neighbour tipped his hat at me. Twice!
Henri, you read the clue so beautifully. Read it again.
I have counted the shutters. All of them open. Lovely!
Seven letters, Henri. "Delight". It fits, and so do we.
Thank you for the cushion, Henri. Where did you find it?
The lemon tree has dropped a leaf in my lap. A gift!
A warm afternoon is a pocket you can keep things in.
Léo waved at me from the fountain! Such a wave!
Camille's dress is the colour of apricots today. Gorgeous.
Henri, the crossword can wait. Look at that cloud!
Shall I hold the paper, Henri? Your hands are on holiday.
There is the breeze again. It always knows where I sit.
I lent Henri my reading glasses. He looks very clever.
Every afternoon this bench gets a little more ours.
The gulls are taking an afternoon nap. Very wise.
Hold my hand, Henri. No reason. It is just a nice hand.
A little girl gave me a daisy just now. I am a queen!
Henri hums when he is thinking. I adore it.
Look at the string lights resting. They work so hard at night.
Everyone who walks by smiles. It must be the weather.
That is the third clue you have let me solve. I see you!
Such a soft afternoon. Like a towel from the line.
Henri, you smell of lemon leaves. Have you been watering?
My feet are in the sun and my hat is in the shade. Bliss.
The cypresses are swaying. Like they heard a waltz.
Four letters, "warm"? Henri, that is the day exactly.
Do you want my scarf, Henri? No? It suits you though.
Bonjour, Madame! What a sweet hat! Is it new?
Henri, mind the step. There. You are a dancer!
Smell that? Someone has baked something with apricots.
Thank you for walking on the windy side, darling.
The promenade is warm right through my shoes. Heaven.
Marcel! The terrace looks wonderful! The flowers too!
Slower, Henri. I want this walk to last till supper.
The jacaranda is dropping petals on us. Like a wedding!
Bonjour, Léo! Bonjour, Léo's friend! Such fast legs!
The breeze has untied my scarf. Henri, would you?
There, Lucie's bicycle by the bakery. The blue one!
Henri, smile at the visitors. They have come so far.
What a warm wall. I could lean on it all afternoon.
You picked a lovely day for a walk, Henri. Clever man.
Arm in arm since nineteen-eighty-something. Still fits.
The palms are whispering. I think they like us.
Stop here, Henri. Just to feel the breeze. Mm. Now on.
The shadows are getting long and elegant. Like Henri.
Thank you, young man, for stepping aside! Such manners!
Henri always walks me past the lemon trees. He knows.
We walk this way every day and it is new every day.
Look at the cat on the step. Bonjour, little sphinx!
Your hand is warm, Henri. The sun has been in your pocket.
A bit of shade, a bit of sun. Henri plans it perfectly.
Tip your hat, Henri, it is the neighbour from the church!
My shoes are new and the promenade approves.
The café chairs are all tucked in. Marcel is so neat.
What a gentle afternoon. Not a single thing out of place.
Have you tried Marcel's lemonade? Sunshine in a glass!
Henri carried my bag all the way. I shall knit him a sock.
This warmth! Like the whole town is a cup of tea.
Everyone has their windows open. You can hear the radios!
The light has gone all honey. The afternoon is ripening.
I said thank you to the fountain. It deserves it.
A kind word costs nothing and the whole town is rich.
Marcel saved me the last madeleine. I have been spoiled!
Oh, the breeze smells of lavender. Someone is ironing.
I complimented a stranger's shoes. Now we are friends!
Léo has three pennies for the fountain. Three wishes! Clever boy!
Look at the fountain catch the sun. Little diamonds, all for free!
Léo is racing his friend round the fountain. Léo wins! Again!
A little girl just waved at me. I waved back twice. Good manners!
Léo says the fountain sings in E flat. He would know!
Children and fountains. They were invented for each other.
A leaf is floating round the fountain. Léo has named it Gérard!
Léo told me the plan. Hopscotch, then fountain, then ice cream!
I count the children at the fountain like Inès counts laps. Five!
Mind the chalk, Henri! Léo drew a rocket on the stones.
Step over the hopscotch, Henri. Number seven is very precious.
Léo's knees are green from the grass. Summer knees! The best kind.
The little ones are feeding the sparrows. The sparrows are delighted!
When I was nine I paddled in that fountain. Twice a day!
Léo just bowed to me. Like a little prince. I curtsied, of course!
The fountain has a rainbow in it at four o'clock. Look, there!
Henri, wake up. No, don't. You look so peaceful.
The bench is exactly the right warmth. Like a loaf from Lucie.
What a gift, an ordinary Tuesday. Or Thursday. A lovely day, anyway!
Forty-one years and he still saves me the shady side. Bless him.
Nothing to do until supper. Isn't that wonderful?
I said hello to eleven people today. Eleven! A good day.
The cypresses are standing so straight. Like they're on parade!
Sun on my hands, Henri beside me. I want nothing at all.
Look at that cloud, Henri. It's a poodle. A very fluffy poodle!
The whole town smells of warm stone and lemons. Heavenly!
Sit, rest, wave at people. My whole job now. I'm very good at it!
Arm in arm, the length of the promenade. Our favourite little trip!
Henri, see the shutters on the blue house? Newly painted! Lovely.
Camille, that dress! Yellow suits you. Like a lemon tree.
Afternoon, Marcel! Your apron is spotless. How do you do it?
Lucie! Mind the gulls, darling. They do love your basket.
Here comes Lucie's bell. Ding! I'd know it anywhere.
The palms are waving at us, Henri. Wave back. There!
Ten steps, then a little rest. Ten more, another little rest!
We walk to the kiosk and back. Exactly one small adventure.
Oh, the café umbrellas are all open. Like a field of flowers!
Henri's cane taps and my shoes click. We make a little song.
Stop a moment, Henri. Just to look. Isn't our town pretty?
Soon the windows will start, one by one. I know the order by heart!
The café lamps aren't lit yet. You can tell they're thinking about it.
In an hour the windows turn to honey. My favourite part of the day!
See the shadows stretching? The afternoon is putting its feet up.
Every window is a little mirror of the sun right now. Dazzling!
I can see my own kitchen window from here. I left a lamp for later.
The kiosk has the evening papers out. Crisp as linen!
The lemon trees cast lemon-shaped shadows. Well, nearly!
Henri has watered that geranium three times. It looks spoiled!
Henri's lemon tree has seven new lemons. He counted. Twice.
There's a cat asleep on the café step. Nobody dares move him!
Every visitor looks so happy to be here. Of course they do!
That young couple shared one ice cream. Two spoons. Adorable!
Théo has been 'working' on the bench for an hour. Bravo, Théo!
Camille is reading on the steps. She turns pages like a cat stretches.
Biscuit had his paws on the fountain edge. Such curiosity!
Yusuf says Biscuit had a busy morning. Now look. Snoring!
I do love the sound of cups at the café. Clink, chatter, clink.
Marcel just dashed past with four lemonades. Not one spilled!
There are sunflowers painted on the kiosk shutter. Very cheerful.
A bee visited my hat. I took it as a compliment!
The bougainvillea is so pink today it's almost showing off.
I knitted on this bench for thirty summers. Scarves for everyone!
Henri brought me a fig. A whole fig! He's very romantic.
Look at the children's chalk. A sun, a cat and a very long dog.
Léo says when he's ten he'll be nearly grown up. Nearly!
Léo asked how old I am. I said 'enough'. He was satisfied.
Les enfants built a castle of café chairs. Marcel allows it!
Léo is teaching the little one to whistle. Mostly it is air!
We pass the fountain on purpose. It's the best bit of the walk.
A coin in the fountain for us, Henri. Same wish as always.
Thank you, sun. Thank you, bench. Thank you, Henri. Merci, everyone!
I like to sit and be grateful for small things. Today: the breeze.
Some afternoons are so gentle you could fold them and keep them.
A quiet half hour, a warm bench. That's a little holiday, you know.
Everyone waves on this promenade. It's catching! I caught it long ago.
I told Henri I love him. He said 'I know, darling. Four letters.'
Good afternoon, little one! Yes, you, with the enormous balloon!
The bell at the church says five. Five o'clock and all is lovely!
When the sun dips there, behind the cypress, it's time for our walk.
Home for a cardigan, Henri? No? Then onwards, my dear!
I am learning a poem by heart. Two verses so far. Henri, test me!
I am practising my watercolours. The sea keeps coming out lilac.
Henri sat very still for my sketch. Then he waved. Now two noses!
I am learning the names of the clouds. That one is a cumulus. Hello!
I am learning to walk backwards like a dancer. Hold on, Henri!
Léo is teaching me to whistle with two fingers. Nearly! Nearly!
Lucie says she will teach me the bicycle bell. Ding, then smile!
A capital O with a little curl. Like a snail in a hat. Elegant!
I learned to fold a paper bird today. It is a little lopsided. Sweet!
I gave the paper bird to a little boy. He flew it straight to Henri.
I am learning Marcel's lemonade recipe. Step one is a secret!
Henri is teaching me the names of his roses. This one is Margot.
That is a stone pine, Henri? Stone pine! I will remember now.
Camille lent me a book about birds. That one is a wagtail! Wag, wag!
The palm shadow touches the kiosk. That means quarter past four!
Was it the queen of hearts? It is always the queen of hearts, Henri.
I practised my tango steps in the kitchen. The kettle applauded.
Tango step, Henri. And turn. And one little dip. Bravo, us!
I am learning the harmony to our song. You sing the tune, Henri.
I learn one new face a day here. Today, the man in blue!
I am learning to play pétanque. Henri says I throw like a poet.
I asked Léo to teach me a skipping rhyme. It has eleven verses!
Learning to sit and do nothing. Henri is a natural. I am improving.
To Lucie! Our bread, our bell, our sunshine. Too much? No, perfect.
I took a photo of the fountain. Henri's thumb is in it. Very artistic!
Henri, look. I have drawn the café. Marcel is the small dot. Waving!
I am learning to say bonjour in Norwegian. God dag! Very sturdy.
Henri ran for my glove and tripped. I married him for that.
He peeled the orange in one long ribbon. I have loved him ever since.
The night they first hung the string lights, everyone clapped. I did!
Henri proposed by the lemon trees. With a lemon! I said yes!
We danced at our wedding right there. Marcel's father played!
My mother sat on this bench too. She waved at everyone. Like me!
Henri painted our front door blue one summer. And his shoes. And me!
The summer of the parade! Henri was a giant sunflower. Superb!
My first ice cream came from that kiosk. Strawberry. Still the best!
Once it rained so warm we all danced in it. Even the mayor!
Remember our picnic on the steps, Henri? Figs, bread and a wasp!
Every year he redraws the chalk heart. Right here. He thinks I forget!
The first time I saw the sea from here, I was six. I said 'more!'
My first bicycle was red. I rang the bell at every single gull.
Henri wrote from Lyon: 'I dream of the bench.' And of me!
Marcel was a tiny boy once, carrying one spoon at a time. So serious!
Camille was once a little girl who sat on my knee for stories.
When the café got striped umbrellas, Henri bought me a matching hat!
We walked this way the day Léo was born. Camille was so proud!
I learned to waltz on these stones. Mama counted. One, two, three!
Henri sang to me under the window once. Off key. My heart sang on key.
I keep a little jar of happy days. Today goes in the jar. Easily!
My diary is all afternoons. Thirty years of very nice afternoons!
Henri is learning to say 'koselig'. He says 'cosy leg'. Close enough!
Practising patience, Henri says. I am patiently waiting for cake.
Henri, the other way round the fountain! Everything looks brand new.
Marcel taught me 'à tout à l'heure' properly. With the little wave.
I am practising looking mysterious. Henri says I look hungry.
Léo is teaching me the planets. Saturn is the one with the hat.
My promenade walk: chin up, scarf out, wave left, wave right!
My first crochet flower! It is a little potato-shaped. I adore it.
Théo says I have a gift for pétanque. Or for talking during pétanque.
Practising my French accent for the visitors. Bonjour! Too much?
Ten thousand walks on this promenade, and I am still learning it!
I learned a new recipe! Apricot clafoutis. Henri is already hungry.
Each afternoon I practise one kindness. Today I fixed a lady's collar!
Henri taught me chess here in the spring. Now I beat him. Gently!
The bougainvillea goes purple at this hour. Look, Henri, purple!
Tomorrow I am taking a cutting of Lucie's geranium. She said yes!
Smell that? Jasmine. It waits all day for the lamps, like me.
My mother kept a lemon tree on a balcony the size of a hat.
A little rosé, and tomorrow, the market. Peaches, I think!
The oleander by the kiosk has three new flowers. I counted!
Bonsoir, little lemons. Sleep well. Grow a bit.
Henri proposed beside a pot of basil. It is still my favourite.
The Lefèvres' window box is all red now. Good for them!
My sister writes that her roses are taller than her husband!
A little wine, a little lamp, a little Henri. Perfect.
There goes the first star, right over the cypress. Hello!
I plan to sit here again tomorrow. Same bench, same husband.
The palm by the fountain has a new frond. Like a green feather!
Marcel, a candle for Henri. He reads the menu by it, darling.
Every window box in town, I could name the flower in it.
Henri, remind me. Seeds for the blue morning glories.
When I was small, my grandmother dried lemon peel on the sill.
We will share the tarte tomorrow. Today, a glass. Balance!
The bougainvillea has climbed one more shutter. Ambitious girl!
Our first flat had one geranium. We called it the garden.
The cypresses look like ink now. Very elegant, all of them.
Rosé the colour of the oleander. I chose it on purpose.
Tomorrow, Henri, we walk to the far end and back. Slowly.
Look how the mimosa folds up for the night. So tidy!
Bonsoir, Yusuf! Bonsoir, Biscuit! Bonsoir, nice lamp!
Henri says the lemon in my glass is from our tree. It is not.
My niece is coming in spring. I shall show her every flower.
This bench, this hour. I would put it in a vase if I could.
The Moreau balcony has a new pot. Pink! I approve.
Marcel's basil on the sill is doing beautifully. Bravo, Marcel!
Plans for tomorrow: coffee, the tarte, and a word with the roses.
Henri carried my mother's fig tree up three flights. A hero!
Half a glass. I am saving the other half for tomorrow.
We planted that lemon tree the year the café got its awning.
Night-scented stock, Henri. Smell. Isn't the town clever?
I shall sit here until the last shutter is lilac. Then home.
The candle, the glass, the geraniums. A still life with Henri.
In the morning, I'll ask Marcel about his rosemary. Secrets!
My father whistled to his tomatoes. They grew enormous.
Look! The fountain has a petal floating in it. Bougainvillea.
We used to dance between these tables. We still might, later!
The jasmine on the post office wall is out. Finally, darling!
Forty-one summers of geraniums. Each one red. Each one new.
Marcel, the little vase on our table. Is that thyme? Clever!
Blue sky, white walls, pink flowers. Who painted this town?
My granddaughter calls the bougainvillea the paper flowers.
Henri, you missed a leaf on the lemon tree. I'm teasing.
To the lemon tree! To the basil! To Henri, mostly.
The palms whisper at this hour. They have such nice manners.
I'm going to press a bougainvillea flower in my recipe book.
Inès stopped to smell the roses. Literally! I saw her.
My mother said: water at dusk, and the plants say thank you.
Every shutter has a pot, every pot has a flower. Lovely town.
The orange tree on the corner has blossom. In this season!
Lamps on. Lemons glowing. Henri humming. Everything's in order.
The geraniums go dark red at this hour. Like good jam.
Lucie's bike basket had sunflowers in it today. Sunflowers!
My aunt grew lemons as big as fists. She was very proud.
Tomorrow morning, Henri and I repot the little olive. Together.
Bonsoir, Lucie! Your window box is the talk of the street!
That climbing rose on the kiosk is older than Marcel's apron.
Henri, the lavender is still humming. The bees went to bed.
Candles on, glasses pink. Marcel makes it look so easy.
The blue hour turns the lemons into little lanterns. Look.
Our wedding bouquet was jasmine and lemon leaves. Smelt divine.
I have plans. Tomorrow I learn the name of that yellow flower.
Henri always orders for me. He has never once been wrong.
The church bell rang and the oleander didn't even blink.
The Lefèvres' cat is asleep in their flower pot again. Sweet!
Sunday we visit your sister's garden, Henri. Don't let me forget!
A sip for the lemon tree, a sip for me. Fair is fair.
There's a gecko on the warm wall. Bonsoir, monsieur gecko!
When Henri retired, he adopted every plant on the street.
The string lights make the palm look dressed for a party.
Marcel trims his basil with scissors. Like a hairdresser!
That bougainvillea has been pink since before we married.
A picnic by the fountain tomorrow. I'll bring the good figs.
My mother's lemon cake. I'll bake it Sunday, Henri. Promise.
The tables in the lamplight look like little islands of gold.
Even the cacti look cosy this evening. Well done, cacti.
Henri named the lemon tree. I won't tell you. It's private!
We'll sit until the candle is half. Then Henri walks me home.
Théo bought flowers for Camille. I saw the paper. Peonies!
The sky has gone the colour of a good blue teapot.
The string lights are on. Somebody blew out the sun.
Blue hour! My favourite hour, and I have checked them all.
The fountain is lit! It looks like it is wearing pearls.
The shutters are closing one by one. Like eyelids!
Madame Roux has closed her green shutters. Eight o'clock, exactly.
That cat on the wall has not moved since lunch. A professional.
There goes Biscuit! He walks like he owns the promenade.
The gulls have gone to bed. Even the noisy one.
One gull is still up. Reading the lamps, I suppose.
The clock says twenty past eight. The sky says lovely.
The church clock and the café clock disagree. Both charming.
Look at the roofs! The zinc has gone all silver and blue.
The whitewash glows at this hour. Like milk in moonlight.
Blue hour, blue shutters, blue tiles. Everything matches!
Every window a little yellow square. Like a box of fudge.
The pink lamp, the yellow lamp, the green one. I know them all!
The baker's light is off. He gets up before the gulls.
Somebody upstairs is playing the piano. Slowly and beautifully.
Someone is cooking garlic. Bless them, whoever they are.
The palms look like they are made of paper now. So elegant.
The cypresses have turned into tall dark exclamation marks!
The kiosk has its little bulb on. Open for one more postcard!
That blue tile by the fountain is my favourite. I say hello to it.
The fountain sounds louder when it gets dark. Have you noticed?
The sea is still pink at the edges. Showing off a little.
Camille and Théo are clinking glasses. Twice! Romantic.
Théo is doing nothing again, and doing it very well.
Yusuf is on the phone to his mother. He always is, at eight.
Every lamp post has its own moth. They have assigned seats.
There, the Moreaus are home. Their curtains are new!
Somebody has hung out a blue tablecloth. It fits the sky.
A window just opened. Somebody wanted to hear the fountain.
The moon is up, but it is being very modest about it.
Is that the same cat or his cousin? They both look smug.
The light from the café makes the cobbles look buttered.
Blue hour. Happy blue! Blueberry blue.
The string lights sway a little. Like they are humming.
Henri, budge up. There. Two old lamps on a bench.
We have sat on this bench so long it knows our shapes.
From this bench I can see four kitchens. Two are having soup.
The bench is still warm from the sun. Like a teacake!
Henri is counting the lit windows. He is at thirty-one.
Thirty-two! Henri, the Lefèvres just turned on the hall.
Sit, sit. The lamps do the rest of the work.
The best seat in town, and nobody sells tickets.
Henri says the slats are numbered. Mine is the lucky one.
A bench, a husband and a lit fountain. I am a rich woman.
We came for the sunset and stayed for the encore.
The sky is putting its blue coat on. Henri, your scarf.
Henri is pretending not to doze. He is a sweet actor.
Five more minutes on the bench, then wine. That is the rule.
Biscuit stopped to sniff my shoe. A great honour, I am told.
The cat came and sat at the end of our bench. A guest!
Look, Henri, the fountain fish has a spotlight now.
That gull is sitting on the lamp post like a little hat.
From here the clock looks like a second moon. Isn't it sweet?
Henri named that star after me. Again. Every year a new one.
I have counted nine pairs of shoes go by. All very nice shoes.
Bonsoir, Camille! What a lovely cardigan. Blue for blue!
Bench, then café. Henri calls it the evening commute.
Henri, the moon. No, the other way. Yes! Hello, moon.
Henri thinks the tiles are grey. They are periwinkle, darling.
Marcel lit our candle first. We are his favourites, shh!
The candle on our table is dancing. It knows the song.
Rosé at blue hour. Pink and blue! Like a christening.
Henri, your glass is fuller than mine. How suspicious.
Table four. Our table. Marcel keeps it like a promise.
The tablecloth has a tiny lemon on it. Henri is delighted.
Santé, Henri! To the lamps, and to whoever lights them.
